text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today after climbing 13% over two weeks, likely due to profit-taking following a sharp rally. The stock surged Friday to $146.51 on the back of geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports sent Brent crude above $109—but gave back a fraction of those gains today as the initial shock wore off.

The broader context: oil prices remain elevated and volatile. Brent crude is trading at $126.55 globally while US oil is at $101.91, a significant spread partly explained by soaring tanker costs (shipping premiums have pushed the real delivered cost of oil roughly $38 higher per barrel). For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices are generally favorable, but the stock's two-week surge suggests most of that good news may already be priced in—today's pullback is a normal correction after such a fast move up.
